name: Motorized Bicycle
description: Missouri's moped: a two- or three-wheeled device with an automatic transmission whose motor produces less than 3 gross brake horsepower (2,250 W) and can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground. It needs a licensed rider but no registration. Electric bicycles are excluded.

restrictions.rule: Two or three wheels and an automatic transmission; pedals aren't required
Its motor produces less than 3 gross brake horsepower (2,250 W) and can't propel it faster than 30 mph on level ground

The definition also caps the motor's cylinder capacity at 50 cc, a gas-engine measure, and excludes electric bicycles by name rather than electric motors, so a pedal-less electric moped within these limits is one
Riders need a valid driver's license; no motorcycle endorsement
Not registered with the Department of Revenue
Not allowed on interstate highways; riding one there, or without a driver's license, is a class C misdemeanor
Must meet the VESC-17 moped construction and equipment standard to be ridden on a street or highway
Treated as a motor vehicle under any homeowners' or renters' insurance policy
